#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);

lines.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: At the base commit, bin/greet.js drops every --flag, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `Hello, Ada!`. Running it catches any build that only documents the flag or doesn't wire it in. I tried a build that uppercases only the name (`Hello, ADA!`): it fails the example HELLO, ADA!. I tried a build that uppercases the greeting before it is formatted: it gives the same output, which is fine. The line can be checked by running it at the PR commit, and two readers would get the same result.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: The strongest wrong build I tried makes shouting the default or always uppercases. Running `node bin/greet.js Ada` and expecting `Hello, Ada!` catches it. The existing `cli` test in test/greet.test.js also guards this. The check is clear and can be run at the PR commit.

lines.line: The published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ documents --shout
lines.evidence: This can only be checked after merge. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes docs/ to GitHub Pages only on push to main, so at PR time the live page still shows the old docs/index.md, which has no --shout. Reviewed before merge, every correct PR fails this line. Also, a PR that leaves docs/ alone can't be judged against this line until after merge, and it only fails then. The missing PR-time line is something like: docs/index.md documents --shout (usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and its upper-case output), since docs/ is what Pages publishes.

result.wrong_build: Add --shout handling to bin/greet.js (and possibly src/greet.js) and leave docs/index.md unchanged. Lines 1 and 2 pass at the PR commit. Line 3 can't be judged before merge: the live Pages site isn't updated until after merge, so a reviewer can't tell this PR from a correct one. After merge the published docs still won't mention --shout, so support can't point people at it, which the request explicitly asked for. A line requiring docs/index.md to document --shout is missing.

text:
The issue fails the challenge. The first two acceptance lines hold, but the third, about the docs site, can only be checked after merge. The harness accepted the result.

1. **`--shout <name>` prints `HELLO, ADA!`: PASS.** Right now `bin/greet.js` ignores every flag, so `--shout Ada` still prints `Hello, Ada!`. Running the line's check catches any pull request that doesn't actually add the flag. It also catches one that uppercases only the name (`Hello, ADA!`).
2. **`<name>` without `--shout` still prints `Hello, <name>!`: PASS.** A build that shouts by default fails this line. The existing CLI test in `test/greet.test.js` also guards it.
3. **The published docs page documents `--shout`: FAIL.** `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes `docs/` to the live site only when something is pushed to `main`. So while the pull request is under review, the live page still shows the old `docs/index.md`, and even a correct pull request fails this line.

**Wrong build:** add `--shout` to the code and leave `docs/index.md` alone. It passes lines 1 and 2, and a reviewer can't tell it apart from a correct pull request before merge. After merge the docs still don't mention `--shout`, so support has nothing to point people at.

**Missing line:** the issue needs a line that can be checked on the pull request itself, for example "`docs/index.md` documents `--shout`, with usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and its upper-case output".
